\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item The specification is $r_{\mathrm{BTC},t} = \alpha + \beta r_{\mathrm{SPY},t} + \delta (r_{\mathrm{SPY},t} \times \mathrm{Post}_t) + \gamma \mathrm{Post}_t + \epsilon_t$ on daily returns with donut dates dropped and Newey--West standard errors, so $\hat\delta$ is the post-listing change in Bitcoin's equity loading estimated directly from returns with no generated-regressor step. This specification has no control group, and it is reported precisely to show what a design without one would have concluded: read on its own, it says Bitcoin's equity beta fell substantially and dates the fall to the listing. The identical model fitted to each of the nine never-listed control coins returns the mean and cross-sectional standard deviation shown in the table, so every crypto asset's equity beta fell over this window and Bitcoin's decline is an unremarkable draw from that distribution. Table~\ref{tab:ddd} differences the common component out.
\end{tablenotes}
